vocabulary.term: How long have you been studying ~?
vocabulary.example: How long have you been studying English?

grammar.point: Present perfect continuous for ongoing study
grammar.point_ko: 진행 중인 학습을 나타내는 현재완료 진행형
grammar.explanation_en: Use present perfect continuous (have/has been + verb-ing) to talk about learning that started in the past and is still happening: 'I have been studying English for two years.' This emphasizes effort and duration, not just the result.
grammar.explanation_ko: 과거에 시작해 지금도 계속되고 있는 학습을 말할 때 현재완료 진행형(have/has been + 동사-ing)을 씁니다: 'I have been studying English for two years.'(2년째 영어를 공부하고 있어요). 결과보다 노력과 기간을 강조합니다.

examples.en: I have been taking a cooking course since January.
She has been preparing for the exam all week.
How long have you been learning to drive?

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: Yes, I passed one last month. I want to improve more, though.

reading.title: Learning a New Skill
reading.text: I have been taking a computer course since March. At first, the assignments were difficult, but I have improved a lot. Last week, I passed an important exam. My goal is to get a certificate by the end of the year. I am proud of how much I have learned.
reading.text_ko: 저는 3월부터 컴퓨터 강좌를 듣고 있어요. 처음에는 과제가 어려웠지만, 많이 향상됐어요. 지난주에는 중요한 시험에 합격했어요. 제 목표는 연말까지 자격증을 따는 거예요. 제가 얼마나 많이 배웠는지 자랑스러워요.

explanation.en: The text says 'I passed an important exam.'
The text says 'to get a certificate by the end of the year.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'get a certificate by the end of the year'라고 나옵니다.
